name: ik_llama.cpp
what: Iwan Kawrakow's fork of llama.cpp, split in mid-2024 and developed on its own since: the IQK quantization types, faster CPU and hybrid CPU/GPU inference for MoE models with experts left in RAM, MLA for DeepSeek, tensor parallel, MTP and DFlash speculation. Its llama-server is llama.cpp's of that era: one model per process, the same /health, /v1/models, /props and /slots; no router mode.

version.note: a build number and commit of its own, not llama.cpp's

detect.note: the executable has llama.cpp's name: a running llama-server is this kind when its path runs through the ik_llama.cpp folder, else mainline. There are no release binaries; it is built from source, so a unit is proposed from a running server (its -m and --port) as for llama.cpp.

can: start a unit with its recorded argv
treat it as loaded while it answers /health
cannot: unload without stopping (one model for the server's life)
router mode (--models-dir): the fork predates it

never: -rtr with experts on the CPU for a model you want prompt processing on the GPU for: it repacks RAM tensors to a CPU-only layout (the README's own warning)
--host 0.0.0.0 without a reverse proxy in front: there is no login

update.note: No releases: the check tells you when main moved; pull and rebuild (cmake --build build --config Release) by hand, then restart the units.

windows: cmake -B build -DGGML_CUDA=ON && cmake --build build --config Release -j (the README has a step-by-step Windows build)

good: a large MoE with the experts in RAM and the rest on one card, at better token rates than mainline for the same file
the IQK quants (IQ4_KS and kin) and repacked R4 files made for it
not: the newest architectures first: mainline gets them weeks or months earlier
mainline's newest GGUF features (its router, some recent quant types)
